assets.caption: Four-camera LiDAR prototype on a trolley. Published experimental hardware; distinct from the flameproof mine device.
assets.original_caption:
Figure 1. Prototype hardware setup on a trolley: Four cameras mounted around the Velodyne Puck
Hi‑Res LiDAR, LiDAR interface box, Intel NUC for data processing and Anker 737 Power Bank for
power supply.

assets.caption: Alignment of LiDAR and SfM point clouds with checkerboard projection validation.
assets.original_caption:
Figure 8. (a) Results of the point cloud registration process: Alignment of the LiDAR points with
the SfM‑generated point cloud. The correspondence score for each object is indicated below the
respective object, representing the percentage of LiDAR points that found matches in the SfM recon‑
struction. (b) Validation of the transformation matrix by projecting LiDAR points onto a checker‑
board plane.
assets.attribution: Ranasinghe, Patra, Banerjee and Raval (2025), Sensors 25, 6582, Figure 8. CC BY 4.0. Figure area extracted from published PDF; panels and caption retained.
assets.change_note: Page cropped to complete figure area; no panel or research result edited.

assets.caption: Raw, enhanced, and temporally smoothed images at 1 lux. All four frames and all three result rows are retained.
assets.original_caption:
Figure 9. Results of low‑light image enhancement on a sequence of images taken at a light level
of 1 lux: displayed for frames 1, 120, 203, and 320. (a) Raw input image set, (b) Images after low‑
light enhancement process, (c) Output after temporal smoothing, with nearly uniform colours across
the frames.
assets.attribution: Ranasinghe, Patra, Banerjee and Raval (2025), Sensors 25, 6582, Figure 9. CC BY 4.0. Figure area extracted from published PDF; panels and caption retained.
assets.change_note: Page cropped to complete figure area; no panel or research result edited.

assets.caption: SLAM reconstruction comparing dark, well-lit, and enhanced dark captures. All camera-contribution regions and comparison panels are retained.
assets.original_caption:
Figure 10. SLAM‑based 3D reconstruction with colour‑coded camera contributions and patch‑wise
visual comparison of (a,b) correspond to the DARK and LIGHT datasets without low‑light enhance‑
ment, and (c) corresponds to the DARK dataset with low‑light enhancement applied.

assets.caption: Face-on rotating apertured-target simulation in Rotating Target Calibration Studio. Noise-free exploration of scan architectures and angle recovery; not measured physical timing accuracy.
assets.attribution: Copyright (c) 2026 Pasindu Ranasinghe, School of Minerals and Energy Resources Engineering, UNSW Sydney, Australia. MIT License.
assets.change_note: Downloaded original PNG unchanged. Complete MIT copyright and permission notice retained alongside the public image.
assets.readme_context: Standalone browser tool for rotating-target geometry, LiDAR/camera architectures, angle estimation and timestamp conventions. README scope states a noise-free scene excluding range noise, classification error, boundary blur and radiometric effects; accuracy is an optimistic bound, not measured hardware performance.
assets.citation: Ranasinghe, P., Patra, D., Banerjee, B. P., and Raval, S. (2026). A Rotating Aperture Target with a Common Geometric Estimator for Temporal Calibration of Heterogeneous Sensors. SSRN preprint. doi:10.2139/ssrn.7513129.
